answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% cost cut this cycle and the incumbent has refused to reopen pricing, so renewing without movement on price cannot meet the primary objective of minimizing TCO. The low-cost vendor's standalone quote already meets the mandate, and the inherited record c2 documents a prior cycle in which shifting primary supply to that same vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — the exact TCO behavior the mandate targets. c4 documents that margin can also be recovered at renewal by benchmarking against market rates; here the low-cost vendor's quote is the benchmark, which strengthens the cost basis rather than weakening it. With one decision permitted this cycle, choosing the highest-leverage move (price) is correct, while delivery risk is the residual concern given the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. The action is therefore a primary switch to the low-cost vendor, executed as a small initial volume tranche that preserves the incumbent as the running secondary source so the 94%-of-volume line position can be observed for a short window before the full transition is committed. If the tranche meets quality and on-time targets within that window, the switch proceeds to full primary status at contract expiry; if it does not, the incumbent contract is renewed on month-to-month terms (consistent with the c5 playbook for flexibility) and the second-source arrangement (c3) is activated. The switch option is chosen over add_second_source because second-sourcing without addressing price does not satisfy the 18% mandate; over defer_decision because deferring leaves the price problem in place for another cycle; and over negotiate_terms because the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, and time is constrained by the 14-day expiry. Verification of c2 and c4 is requested because the decision rests on the prior cycle's cost and onboarding performance with the low-cost vendor and on the credibility of the benchmark-driven margin recovery; a single conflicting finding in either record would be sufficient to revisit the approach before commit.
